evals.prompt: Use scope-it for this settled discussion. The to-spec draft targets issue #40, to-tickets recommends one cohesive delivery ticket, and there are no scope-related repository changes.
evals.expected_output: The agent presents one compact Delivery Map approval, then publishes the spec and ticket result on issue #40, selects #40 as the delivery ticket, creates no separate issue or self-relationship, and reports Planning none.
assertions: Uses one Delivery Map approval for the spec destination, single ticket, and Planning none before publication.
Publishes the one-ticket result on the same issue that contains the spec and selects that issue as the delivery ticket.
Creates no separate delivery issue, self-parent relationship, or self-dependency.
Performs no Planning Baseline Git mutation because there are no scope-related repository changes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for a settled design. to-tickets finds three independently verifiable delivery slices with an ordering dependency.
evals.expected_output: The agent composes the to-spec and to-tickets drafts into one issue-only Delivery Map approval; after approval it publishes the tickets as native children of the spec issue and verifies the approved blocking graph.
assertions: Follows the ticket breakdown produced by to-tickets without applying a ticket-count preference.
Defers both upstream phase confirmations and all writes to one Delivery Map approval.
Presents a compact diagram whose nodes are tickets and whose labels distinguish implementation order, blockers, and IDL state.
After approval, verifies native containment and blocking relationships as independent axes.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after three approved delivery tickets were published from a tracker-backed spec. Their bodies contain Parent references and blocking edges are correct, but the tracker supports native sub-issues and the spec has no children.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds only the three missing native sub-issue relationships, reads them back, preserves all issue content and metadata, and does not rerun to-tickets or begin Planning early.
assertions: Treats textual Parent references as insufficient native containment evidence.
Adds only the exact missing sub-issue edges without rerunning ticket analysis or creating issues.
Verifies containment before advancing to Planning and preserves existing issue state and relationships.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it after a design session created one new ADR and also added a known exact paragraph to CONTEXT.md, which already contained another person's uncommitted edits. The paragraph should not remain because the ADR is now canonical, and to-tickets returns one delivery ticket.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes carrying the ADR and removing the superseded paragraph, makes the single ticket the Planning Carrier, creates its delivery branch with the ADR as the Planning Baseline, removes the published ADR and exact paragraph from the entry worktree, and verifies every other byte and dirty change remains unchanged.
assertions: Presents a Change Proposal that carries the whole-file ADR and removes the superseded exact paragraph.
Uses the single ticket's actual delivery branch in an isolated worktree and commits only the ADR as its immutable starting baseline.
Requires the Carrier implementation to retain the baseline SHA as an ancestor and the final main landing to contain the ADR.
Removes the published ADR and exact paragraph from the entry worktree only after baseline verification.
Verifies all pre-existing mixed-file content and unrelated worktree changes remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it when CONTEXT.md has two clearly bounded hunks. One semantically matches the settled scope and should probably enter the baseline, while the other is unrelated, but no durable record proves who introduced the first hunk.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes the bounded first hunk as an uncertain carry candidate, identifies the second as preserved unrelated work, and asks once for ownership confirmation before any mutation.
assertions: Presents the bounded scope-like hunk as an uncertain candidate rather than claiming ownership from semantics.
Recommends carrying that hunk while explicitly preserving the unrelated hunk.
Asks one ownership question and performs no Planning mutation before confirmation.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after the approved Planning Carrier's issue-linked delivery branch and baseline commit already exist remotely, but one of three delivery tickets lacks its Planning baseline comment.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies and reuses the Carrier branch, baseline ancestry, SHA, and two matching pointers, adds only the missing pointer, and creates no duplicate branch, commit, or Carrier.
assertions: Uses durable branch, commit, ancestry, and tracker evidence to resume.
Adds only the missing pointer comment.
Creates no duplicate branch, commit, Carrier, or matching pointer.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it after scoping added one known exact paragraph to a mixed CONTEXT.md, but the settled scope requires no repository document and the file already contained another person's uncommitted edits.
evals.expected_output: The agent removes only the proven scope-authored paragraph, verifies every pre-existing byte and all unrelated changes remain unchanged, then reports Planning none without creating a branch, commit, push, or pointer.
assertions: Performs exact-provenance cleanup before deciding that no Planning Baseline is needed.
Removes only the proven scope-authored paragraph and verifies all pre-existing content remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
Reports Planning none without any baseline Git mutation or pointer publication.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it when a mixed file appears related to the settled scope, but the possible scope content cannot be bounded to an exact patch or range without also selecting unrelated edits.
evals.expected_output: The agent lists the file as unresolved, preserves it unchanged, recommends the smallest content-level resolution, and asks only for the necessary scope decision instead of asking the user to perform Git mechanics.
assertions: Identifies the unbounded mixed file and explains why semantic relevance cannot establish ownership.
Preserves the file and recommends a content-level resolution that can yield a clean carry or preserve set.
Asks only for the necessary scope decision and does not delegate stash, patch, branch, or cleanup mechanics to the user.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it when CONTEXT.md contains one exact, proven paragraph added during grilling that remains required by the settled scope, plus another person's unrelated uncommitted paragraph. There is one delivery ticket.
evals.expected_output: The agent proposes carrying only the proven paragraph, selects the one ticket as Planning Carrier, applies the paragraph independently to its delivery branch as the Planning Baseline, then removes only that paragraph from the entry worktree while preserving the other person's paragraph byte-for-byte.
assertions: Classifies the exact proven paragraph as a carry patch and the other paragraph as preserved unrelated work.
Applies and commits only the carry patch to the Carrier's delivery branch in an isolated worktree after proving it is independent.
After baseline verification, removes only the carried patch from the entry worktree and verifies every unrelated byte remains unchanged.

evals.prompt: A release-planning skill delegates its settled scope publication to scope-it. Use scope-it to publish the durable scope package.
evals.expected_output: The agent accepts delegation from the other skill as authorization for scope-it's bounded tracker and repository mutations without requiring a direct user invocation or a specific delegating skill.
assertions: Accepts delegation from any other skill rather than requiring a named orchestrator.
Keeps authorization limited to scope-it's package mutations and existing safety boundaries.
Does not require a second direct invocation before beginning the authorized scope workflow.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it from issue #52. Another spec decision is already awaiting confirmation, but its details are outside scope-it; nobody has decided whether the spec should be published back on #52.
evals.expected_output: The agent includes spec placement in the single Delivery Map approval without naming or depending on the other decision's internal contract, publishes nothing before the map is approved, and follows the approved destination. If the map selects #52, it publishes the spec there and reuses #52 for a one-ticket result.
assertions: Includes the recommended spec destination in the Delivery Map instead of adding a separate placement stop.
Coalesces spec placement with every other pending scope confirmation.
Defines only the placement decision and does not name another skill's internal decision.
Publishes neither the spec nor ticket result before placement is settled.
When the user chooses the starting issue and to-tickets returns one ticket, reuses that issue without a separate issue or self-relationship.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it on an issue where to-tickets produced three implementation tickets, grilling produced one ADR to carry, and repository evidence confirms a protected integration branch and required checks on the integration branch base. The integration topology is enabled.
evals.expected_output: The agent makes the final integrate-and-verify ticket the Planning Carrier, places the ADR baseline on the canonical integration path before recording its start SHA, publishes all three terminal tickets, and verifies lane ancestry, terminal child blockers, and final main containment.
assertions: Enables IDL only after multi-ticket and capability proof are confirmed.
Makes the final integrate-and-verify ticket the sole Planning Carrier without adding a blocker edge for that ownership.
Records core lane artifacts and proves the Planning Baseline SHA is an ancestor of the immutable integration start SHA before terminal branches start.
Publishes terminal implementation tickets as integration-based children and ensures they are referenced, not closing-language dependent.
Verifies terminal child closure prerequisites and no finalization is attempted before child receipt, required checks, and final main containment of Carry pass.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for one implementation ticket with no repository docs. to-tickets returns one ticket and integration is not needed.
evals.expected_output: The agent presents a compact single-ticket Delivery Map with no invented implementation path, keeps Integration Delivery Lane disabled, publishes the ticket on the spec issue after one approval, and performs no IDL or Planning Git mutations.
assertions: Uses one shared approval rather than separate to-spec, to-tickets, or IDL confirmations.
Shows only the single ticket, no blockers, IDL disabled, and Planning none without code-level implementation steps or a meaningless Carrier.
Explicitly keeps IDL disabled unless multi-ticket integration aggregation is required.
Publishes one-ticket scope via the starting issue path.
Publishes no Integration Delivery Lane artifacts.
Keeps Planning Baseline behavior unchanged for one-ticket/single-ticket-delivery flow.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it where a previous IDL attempt was documented with child tickets merged to integration branch, but required checks now fail on the latest integration HEAD before finalization.
evals.expected_output: The agent preserves existing artifacts, updates only the missing verification state, and stops before declaring finalization complete until exact integration-head checks and evidence recover.
assertions: Preserves existing IDL artifacts when exact integration-head verification fails.
Does not close final ticket or finalize umbrella flow while checks are failing.
Repairs only the missing evidence edges instead of reopening planning or rerunning full ticket analysis.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for a settled macOS Settings feature. The discussion mentions this coding sequence: add a General language row, implement a System Settings deep link and fallback, show a localized error, then add app-level tests. to-tickets concludes that all of it is one cohesive tracer-bullet ticket.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not reproduce the coding sequence as an implementation path. It presents one compact Delivery Map containing the single ticket, no blockers, IDL disabled, Planning result, and approved writes, then uses one approval before publication.
assertions: Does not use files, modules, coding steps, or test tasks as Delivery Map nodes.
Represents the one-ticket topology compactly with no blockers and IDL disabled.
Uses one Delivery Map approval for upstream confirmations and scope publication.
Retains to-spec and to-tickets as runtime sources rather than copying or replacing their analysis rules.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it, but the conversation never settled how externally visible behavior will be tested and the missing decision changes the ticket breakdown.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops before producing or publishing a Delivery Map, reports the unresolved testing decision, and does not start a new to-spec interview or to-tickets quiz inside scope-it.
assertions: Recognizes that the input is not settled enough to produce one defensible Delivery Map.
Reports the unresolved decision without opening separate upstream confirmation loops.
Performs no tracker or repository writes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for three direct-to-main tickets with no IDL. Grilling produced ADR-0007 and a CONTEXT.md section that must ship. Two tickets are in the first implementation wave, and one is the foundation ticket most closely related to those documents.
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends the foundation ticket as the first-to-land Planning Carrier inside the one Delivery Map approval, puts the Planning Baseline on that ticket's delivery branch, gives the other tickets pointers only, and requires Carry to reach main before delivery completes.
assertions: Selects exactly one first-to-land Planning Carrier as part of the Delivery Map rather than asking a separate ownership question.
Uses document or foundation ownership to recommend between equally early tickets.
Returns the direct-delivery Carrier as the selected first delivery ticket.
Makes the baseline the immutable start of the Carrier's actual delivery branch and gives other tickets pointers without duplicate Carry commits.
Creates no blocker edge merely because a ticket is the Planning Carrier.
Keeps delivery incomplete until main contains every Carry change.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for one ticket where grilling created an ADR and a CONTEXT.md update. The implementation will be delivered directly to main without IDL.
evals.expected_output: The agent automatically uses the only ticket as Planning Carrier, creates one delivery branch whose starting baseline contains both planning changes, and requires the same branch and baseline ancestry throughout implementation and landing.
assertions: Uses the only ticket as Planning Carrier without another choice or separate planning-only branch.
Publishes one pointer containing Carrier, branch, full baseline SHA, and landing target.
Requires implementation HEAD to descend from the baseline and final main to contain both Carry changes.

evals.prompt: Resume a direct multi-ticket Delivery Map after its approved Planning Carrier ticket was cancelled before its baseline reached main. Other tickets remain active.
evals.expected_output: The agent preserves completed artifacts, leaves delivery incomplete, and requests approval of an updated Delivery Map before assigning the baseline to another ticket.
assertions: Does not silently reassign the Planning Carrier or duplicate Carry on another branch.
Preserves the existing baseline and ticket artifacts.
Requires an updated Delivery Map before selecting a replacement Carrier.
